data_sources: VisText-Mosquito (Mendeley Data): photos of breeding-site objects, used to train the object detector
Stagnant Water and Wet Surface Dataset (Mendeley Data): used to train the visible-water detector
Open-Meteo: rainfall, temperature and humidity (past 7 days and 7-day forecast)
OpenStreetMap: water bodies, drains and construction sites near each cell
Citizen reports submitted through this app

metrics.name: Object detector (Model 1) mAP50
metrics.note: Test split of VisText-Mosquito, 5 classes (tyre, drain inlet, vase/flowerpot, bottle, coconut shell). Same photo source as training, so likely optimistic for Malaysian scenes.

metrics.name: Visible-water detector (Model 2) mAP50
metrics.note: Low because water has no clear edges and the labels are overlapping boxes. Used only as soft evidence that water may be present.

metrics.name: Risk map
metrics.note: Not trained or validated. Weights are assumptions from Aedes ecology. Confidence is never above medium until compared with iDengue hotspots.

metrics.name: Malaysian photo test
metrics.note: Run evaluate_my_photos.py and fill this in.

limitations: Detects possible breeding sites, not larvae or mosquitoes. An officer must verify.
No bucket or drum class yet.
Visible water is not proof that water is stagnant.
